title: GitLab releases critical security patches 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6, 19.2.9, 19.1.9, 19.0.10 and 18.11.13, urging self-managed users to upgrade immediately
content_md:
GitLab releases critical security patch releases 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6, 19.2.9, 19.1.9, 19.0.10 and 18.11.13, covering fixes for multiple high-risk vulnerabilities, and urges self-managed users to upgrade immediately.

The 19.5.1 release fixes CVE-2026-110264, an integer overflow in the regular expression compiler that under certain conditions allows an unauthenticated user to run arbitrary code on the GitLab server. The flaw is rated CVSS 10.0 and affects every GitLab release from 7.0 up to the fixed versions, so the backports to 18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9 and 19.2.9 matter for older installations. The same release also fixes CVE-2026-15723, an OmniAuth to LDAP auto-linking authentication flaw rated 8.2, and CVE-2026-112212, an OAuth and OIDC discovery cache poisoning flaw rated 7.5, plus ten further issues of medium or lower severity. GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already patched. The patch includes database migrations, so single-node instances take downtime during the upgrade.
